howItWorks.heading: How Adulis works
howItWorks.sub: A buyer-facing explanation of the loop—from the seller's social bio to a recorded handoff.

steps.title: The seller shares their shop
steps.body: One Adulis link in their TikTok or Instagram bio.

steps.title: The buyer sees the real thing
steps.body: Seller identity, verification status, trust level, completed order count, live stock and when it was last confirmed.

steps.title: Identity starts in the app
steps.body: Browsing needs no account. A buyer signs in with their phone the first time they reserve.

steps.title: The buyer pays the seller directly
steps.body: Adulis shows the seller's bank details. The buyer transfers and uploads the receipt. The seller checks their own bank account and confirms.

steps.title: The handoff becomes a record
steps.body: The item changes hands, the handoff is confirmed by QR scan, and the order becomes a record both sides can point to.

items.title: Paste the post link
items.body: Copy the TikTok or Instagram post and paste it into the app; it resolves to that seller's tagged products.

howItWorks.moneyBody: Adulis never holds or processes buyer money and never decides whether a transfer is genuine. It records the buyer's receipt upload and the seller's confirmation.

trust.heading: Trust & Safety
trust.sub: These are the mechanics that make buying from someone you follow accountable.

boundaries.title: Never holds buyer money
boundaries.body: Adulis never holds or touches buyer money.

boundaries.title: Never authenticates payment
boundaries.body: Adulis never verifies whether a payment is genuine.

boundaries.title: Never labels a seller
boundaries.body: Adulis never labels a seller good, bad, safe or risky.

verification.title: Proven control of a real social account
verification.body: The seller proves control of a real TikTok or Instagram account.

verification.title: Government ID where required
verification.body: Government ID is used where required.

ladder.meaning: Limited published products · new-seller badge · transaction value cap.

ladder.earnedBy: A sustained run of scanned handoffs with good ratings
ladder.meaning: Full catalogue for the plan · cap lifted.

ladder.earnedBy: Sustained volume, high scan completion, low claims

ladderNotes.title: Levels fall as well as rise
A level is never purchasable
ladderNotes.body: No plan, payment or advertising spend moves a seller up.

ladderNotes.title: Large following does not skip New
ladderNotes.body: A seller with a large following and no sales starts at New, exactly like everyone else.

trust.ladderUndecided: Trust-ladder thresholds are not set yet. When set they are published, never secret.
trust.publishNote: These are counted from Adulis's own records. There is no free-text field, and no opinion is published about anyone.

reviews.title: Reviews always publish
reviews.body: A confirmed handoff earns the strongest badge; refusing to confirm does not remove the review.

reviews.title: Separate ratings
reviews.body: Item quality and seller quality are rated separately and never averaged.

claims.title: What can be claimed
claims.lead: A buyer can raise a claim when:
items: payment was confirmed and the seller did not respond in time
the seller cancelled because stock was not kept current
goods did not arrive after payment
goods were materially not as described
a promised refund was not delivered

claims.title: Outcome
claims.body: A claim can be upheld or not upheld, including bad-faith claims.

claims.title: Evidence export
claims.body: Adulis produces an evidence export and does not file police reports.

moderation.title: Report-and-takedown
moderation.body: Reported content can be reviewed and taken down.

moderation.title: Audit trail
moderation.body: Moderation actions are recorded in an audit trail.

moderation.title: Reasoning privacy
moderation.body: Moderation reasoning is never disclosed to third parties.

prohibited.heading: Prohibited products
prohibited.sub: What may not be sold through Adulis.

categories.title: Illegal goods
categories.body: Products whose sale, possession or distribution is prohibited by law.

categories.title: Stolen goods
categories.body: Items obtained without the lawful owner's permission or right to sell.

categories.title: Counterfeit goods
categories.body: Imitations presented as genuine branded or authenticated products.

categories.title: Fraudulent goods
categories.body: Products offered through false claims, fabricated provenance or deceptive representation.

categories.title: Exploitative goods
categories.body: Items whose production, sale or distribution involves exploitation or abuse.

categories.title: Firearms, ammunition, explosives and prohibited weapons
categories.body: Weapons and weapon-related products that are prohibited or restricted from sale.

categories.title: Illegal drugs and unauthorised controlled substances
categories.body: Drugs or controlled substances sold without lawful authorisation.

categories.title: Sexual exploitation material
categories.body: Material involving sexual exploitation, coercion or abuse.

categories.title: Prohibited hazardous goods
categories.body: Dangerous materials that cannot lawfully or safely be sold, transported or handled.

categories.title: Intellectual-property-infringing products
categories.body: Products that unlawfully copy, reproduce or use someone else's protected rights.

categories.title: Anything barred by local law or an applicable foreign jurisdiction
categories.body: A product may be prohibited because a law applying to the seller, buyer or transaction bars it.

categories.title: Anything barred by a payment or logistics partner, or by Adulis policy
categories.body: Some products cannot be supported because a required partner or Adulis policy does not permit them.

prohibited.noteBody: Adulis uses report-and-takedown and safety suspension.

about.heading: Why we're building Adulis
about.sub: The company story for sellers, investors, accelerators and grant reviewers.
about.originBody: Naod Solomon spent three years running a shop selling through TikTok and Instagram—roughly eighty orders a month through direct messages, against almost nothing on the classifieds sites everyone recommends. The pattern was clear: people follow a seller for months, want a real product from that seller, and then have to finish the purchase inside a DM thread. Adulis is being built around that reality.
